items.title: I've started my first two batches! They started fermenting just 1.5 hours into being bottled. Is that normal? Seems fast.
items.text: I've started my first two batches! They started fermenting just 1.5 hours into being bottled. Is that normal? Seems fast.

Description of my first ever mead batch:

Here, I have two 1 gallon carboys. Each carboy has 2.2 lbs of honey, half of an apple, champagne yeast and yeast nutrient. I got an ABV reading of about 10.5%, which would get me roughly 7% give or take post-fermentation. I have much to learn but im beyond *stoked* for finally getting my first batches setup and fermenting so quickly.

Yup. Just posted my first batch. 70 degrees exactly, yeast nutrient, chamagne yeast, half of an aople diced and added to each one gallon batch with 2.2 lbs of honey for each batch. Its started fermenting almost one bubble every second in the first hour...

No, i didn't start the yeast at all. I microwaved honey *just* enough to make it runny, poured in honey, poured in water. Then i closed the carboys, shook them both to hell, pitched yeast and put on my airlocks. About 1:20, i checked them and theyre bubbling just around once a second.
I used a full packet of champagne yeast. I believe its attenuation is about 19% or something, I forget.
Beautiful color! Im gonna go for a flavor similar to this when i get more familiar with making my own mead.
Gorgeous!

Make sure your bung is super clean and dry, then do the same with the mouth on your carboy. Insert the plug with a fair amount of force while wiggling your hand and pushing down onto it in a circular motion. Then install your airlock. This ensures that the plug is as far down as it can go without the airlock. Once you pu the airlock in, it presses even harder against the inside of the mouth of your container. I did this with mine, not a single issue. Its very important both surfaces are extremely clean and dry for it to grip well.
Yeast nutrient. It takes a few minutes to dissolve. Its not visible at this point anymore though.
Back-sweetening.
1 tsp per gallon as directed.
Right, that's why im saying it wont be that full post ferment ABV because im making a pretty decently sweet batch and one dry batch.
Thanks! Yeah i used one packet for each gallon. Oops lol.

Checked this morning, its going super smooth and the color is very nice so far. Smells amazing as well.

items.title: My first batch ever is finally bottled and put in the fridge! Such an exciting feeling.
items.text: My first batch ever is finally bottled and put in the fridge! Such an exciting feeling.
Holy shit... that's impressive as hell.
Lol
Everytime i brew, i add yeast nutrients. It kickstarted my brew hardcore and my first batch was ready to stabilize and rack in 6 days. I bottled it a day later.
Yup. My EC-1118 ripped my batchcto shreds in a week. It was awesome and it tastes great.
Its about 8 days old. Day 6 fermentation got campden, bentonite and potassium sorbate. Let sit, stabilize for 30 hours cold. Racked over once, sat again, bottled.
It wasnt fermenting at all when i bottled. It was cold crashed for well over a full day, on top of the bisulfate, campden and bentonite, then bottled.

For anyone concerned about bottle bombs; here is the whole process and ingredients

-One gallon fermenter
One pack of EC-1118 yeast
2.2lbs of raw clover honey
One half of an apple diced
Yeast nutrient

This brew fermented extrenely fast. I stopped it only 6 days in with campden and bisulfate. I also cold crashed it at the same time to pretty nearly guarantee no more fermentation. I racked it over once, continued chilling. Another day passed and i racked it over again. Its roughly about 8% ABV, as i wanted to make a slightly weaker/sweeter beer strength batch. Im very new and this was more or less just experimenting for me. It tastes awesome and the apples flavor is perfect. I cant see why id have problems with it. Thank you everyon for your concerns, however.

I never backsweetened because i intentionally cut this batch short so i didnt need to buy more honey. Its just easier for me personally. I stabilized with bisulfate and campden tablets all while cold crashing immediately after adding those products. Alot of people are worried about bottle bombs, maybe they assumed i took no measures to stop fermentation. Its about 8%ABV.

This was a super short brew with EC!1118 yeast. It got me to 8%ABV in a hair under a week. Its pretty sweet, of course. 6 days brewings, bottled at 8. My other batch is going to ferment completely dry. Im new as well, so im experimenting with how quickly i can make mead, what works best, etc.
Yeah its going great! It made racking SO much cleaner the first day in the fridge. However, i have much to learn and this certainly wasnt the best to do it, but it worked.

I gotcha. Thanks for the help. Im *brand new* with this stuff. Im just trying all sorts of things. Itll sit in the fridge for quite a long time, if that means anything to ya. Worst come the worst, ill have to just rack the bottles, then re-bottle everything i suppose. My other batch is just gonna sit and ferment completely dry, of which i just racked, so hopefully no rookie mistakes with that one.
Ah, shit.... thats awkward. Thanks for the tips. It helps alot. Im sure ill learn the hard way soon enough.
Looks like im going down that path... i made it sweet on purpose to see what its like. Its my first batch ever bottled and i learned alot and still have much to learn...
Yeaaah... so im pretty much screwed. Unless i keep it cold or put back into a jug.
